summary.text: A 4-year-old girl presented with bloody stools for 5 days, abdominal pain for 4 days and fever for 3 days, and the abstract adds oliguria. Examination showed periorbital edema, abdominal distension, decreased skin turgor and grade 3 pretibial pitting edema. Initial laboratory results included a platelet count of 57.0×10^(3)/μL, creatinine 1.44 mg/dL, positive schistocytes and stool PCR detecting verotoxin-producing Escherichia coli. Typical HUS was suspected.

She did not respond to hydration and diuretic therapy, and intermittent hemodialysis was started on hospital day 3 for worsening renal function and fluid overload. A generalized tonic-type seizure occurred on hospital day 5, with no remarkable abnormalities on computed tomography or electroencephalography. Urine output rose from anuria to oliguria by hospital day 8, and hemodialysis was discontinued on day 9. Blood dyscrasia improved with repeated hemodialysis and red blood cell transfusions.

On hospital day 15 she had mild right conjunctival swelling and yellowish pus without visual problems. Examination found an internal hordeolum or chalazion (the source names both) and a bilateral retinal hemorrhage. Fundus photography showed hourglass preretinal hemorrhages and a right cotton wool spot, OCT showed bilateral sub-ILM hemorrhages, and best-corrected visual acuity was 20/50 right and 20/25 left without subjective visual symptoms.

Fundus examinations were repeated every 2 weeks and brain MRI and angiography were done to rule out Terson syndrome with no abnormal findings. The right sub-ILM hemorrhage resolved by week 10 with normal capillary plexus on OCTA, the left eye showed healthy capillaries with a focal remnant, and acuity improved to 20/16 in both eyes. She was discharged on day 14 with outpatient follow-up; kidney function is now normal and neurological symptoms are stable.
